summary: Engine-independent map cluster button with compact count formatting and a hover or focus caption.
useWhen: An application map needs one interactive marker to represent several nearby entities.
The map engine can mount a custom element and retain ownership of clustering, coordinates, anchoring, and camera behavior.
avoidWhen: The marker represents one vehicle, asset, person, or travel group; use MapEntityMarker.
The marker represents one application-defined point, location, or event; use MapMarker.
The count is a notification attached to another control; use Badge.
The component would be asked to calculate clusters or own geographic and selected-entity business state.

alternatives.when: One application-defined point needs semantic intent color and an arbitrary map icon.
alternatives.reason: MapMarker owns single-point and event marker semantics and geometry.

alternatives.when: One map entity needs operating state, bearing, and an optional dashed outline.
alternatives.reason: MapEntityMarker owns single-entity marker semantics and geometry.

alternatives.when: A count supplements another non-map control.
alternatives.reason: Badge owns compact notification and counter indicators.

accessibility: The component renders a native button and label is its accessible action name. Prefer a label that includes the full count and outcome, such as ‘Zoom to 24 vehicles’.
Caption is a supplemental visual identifier and is hidden from assistive technology to avoid duplicating label.
Keyboard focus reveals the same caption as hover and uses the shared visible focus ring.
The compact displayed count does not replace the full count in label.
states: count is rounded to a non-negative whole number and compacts with a k suffix at one thousand and above.

dimmed is visual de-emphasis only. The map owner decides when selection context should dim cluster peers and keeps every cluster operable. A dimmed cluster returns to full opacity while hovered or keyboard-focused so its revealed caption remains legible.
Activation emits dsClick without calculating a cluster expansion or changing camera state internally.
responsiveBehavior: Marker height and minimum width stay fixed across breakpoints so map-engine anchors remain stable; width grows only for the compact count.
The map owner controls collision handling, overlays, and viewport-aware caption placement.

customElements: A map engine that accepts an Element for a custom marker or div icon can mount ds-map-cluster-marker directly.
Listen for dsClick and keep cluster membership, expansion zoom, z-index, coordinates, and camera movement in application state.
react: Pass count as a number and handle dsClick through the generated event binding.
angular: Bind count as a number and keep map-engine marker lifecycle in the owning map adapter.

styling.rationale: The component owns stable map anchoring geometry and semantic cluster recipes; the map engine owns host placement and stacking.

protected.reason: Cluster geometry, count legibility, interaction treatment, and de-emphasis are one accessible visual recipe.
